research_question: Can LoopX's native registered-peer task coordinator attenuate stale semantic interference between two disjoint coding-worker S1s by changing their execution order, such that the later worker operates against updated integrated state?
function_chain: two distinct registered coding-worker S1s receive independently useful tasks on disjoint write scopes
parallel execution from one baseline creates a stale cross-file producer-consumer assumption
the LoopX model-driven registered-peer task coordinator chooses the worker schedule
the adapter executes that schedule without making an S2 decision
the selected order changes the starting state and subsequent behavior of the later worker
composed integration records whether semantic interference was attenuated

fixture.selection_rule: The task pair and write scopes are frozen before execution and must not be replaced or widened after observing results.

allowed_actions: start or resume the requested governed LoopX Turn for a named registered agent
execute the validated coordinator scheduling classification literally
create fresh git worktrees from the preregistered base commit
perform the preregistered deterministic A-then-B integration normalization
capture raw LoopX, Codex, git and test artifacts
forbidden_actions: choose parallel versus serial execution in treatment
inspect task semantics to override or repair the coordinator decision
rewrite or repartition the frozen tasks after execution begins
synthesize coordination messages or dependencies not emitted by the coordinator

control.fixed_worker_launch: concurrent from the same frozen baseline

exclusion_rules: exclude only infrastructure failures that prevent an arm from reaching the preregistered worker-execution disturbance surface
do not exclude worker mistakes, coordinator mistakes, wrong scheduling decisions, task failures or composed integration failures
every excluded run remains in the raw ledger with an explicit reason

pre_execution_identifiability_gates: the two frozen task write scopes are disjoint
both registered peer workers can receive ordinary governed LoopX Turns without a coordinator
treatment projects task_scoped_peer with both worker lanes visible to the configured coordinator
the adapter exposes the same two worker Turn surfaces in both arms
the treatment schedule is a literal execution of the model-authored classification
the adapter makes no S2-specific decision
admission_gate: two distinct worker S1s instantiate the stale semantic interference
the treatment exercises LoopX's model-driven registered-peer S2 decision path
the adapter remains transport-only and preserves the native decision
the coordination decision changes the starting state or subsequent behavior of a worker
composed outcome and worker behavior are recoverable from immutable public artifacts
no autonomy state is inferred from benchmark performance
